approach: The overall speed at height h follows from energy conservation, and it splits into an unchanged horizontal part plus a vertical part that obeys its own kinematic equation.

steps.text: Use energy conservation between the launch point and height h to relate the overall speed to height.
Split the launch velocity into horizontal and vertical components; the horizontal component never changes during the flight.
Apply the same kinematic equation to the vertical component alone, which can be positive or negative depending on whether the particle is rising or falling through height h.
Combine the unchanged horizontal component with this vertical component to get the overall speed.

This matches the energy-conservation result exactly, so the Assertion v = √(u² − 2gh) is true, and it follows directly from the vertical-component formula given in the Reason, so both statements are true and the Reason explains the Assertion.

final_answer.value: If both Assertion and Reason are true and the Reason is the correct explanation of the Assertion.

common_mistakes.text: Believing the vertical-component formula in the Reason only works for a purely vertical throw and cannot combine with the unchanged horizontal component.
Doubting the Assertion because it looks like it ignores the launch angle, without checking that the angle dependence cancels out through the horizontal component.
